title: An Ising machine for combinatorial optimization based on sub-nanosecond CMOS-integrated magnetoresistive random-access memory
task: Develop CMOS-integrated spintronic Ising machine for combinatorial optimization with sub-nanosecond updates
key_results: Sub-nanosecond probabilistic spin updates (0.3–1 ns); energy efficiency <40 fJ per spin; 96,000 integrated spins; solves Max-cut and electronic design automation problems (global routing, layer assignment); system energy efficiency 1.92 × 10⁵ solutions/second/watt
comments: Voltage-controlled magnetic anisotropy provides tunable switching probability and low write current, but current noise floor and thermal fluctuations may limit practical problem sizes compared to simulated performance.

model_io.model: CMOS-integrated magnetoresistive random-access memory (MRAM) Ising machine with voltage-controlled magnetic anisotropy
inputs: combinatorial optimization problem (Max-cut, global routing, layer assignment)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Voltage-controlled magnetic anisotropy enables tunable single-pulse switching probability and sub-nanosecond spin updates
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; 0–100% switching probability achievable via pulse-width control; spin update speed 0.3–1 ns demonstrates viability of fast hardware Ising implementation

hypotheses.hypothesis: On-chip all-to-all coupling via integrated spintronic array provides scalable solution to industry-relevant combinatorial problems
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; demonstrated on Max-cut benchmarks and EDA problems with 1.92 × 10⁵ solutions/second/watt energy efficiency

title: A Rydberg atomic synthetic-aperture radar imaging system approaching the Rayleigh criterion
task: Develop Rydberg atomic synthetic-aperture radar imaging approaching Rayleigh criterion resolution
key_results: Omni-SAR achieves millimetre-scale broadband microwave imaging resolution approaching Rayleigh criterion; isotropic, polarization-independent response to incident field magnitude from degenerate π and σ± Rydberg transitions; accesses k-space regions inaccessible to conventional antenna-based SAR
comments: Rydberg atomic receiver overcomes polarization-dependent antenna constraints elegantly, but bandwidth limitations and scalability to imaging large areas or high operating frequencies require further development.

model_io.model: Rydberg atomic quantum receiver (electromagnetically induced transparency with Autler–Townes splitting)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Isotropic and polarization-independent Rydberg atomic response enables access to k-space regions forbidden to antenna-based SAR
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; degenerate π and σ± transitions in alkali ensemble yield isotropic response, allowing Omni-SAR to approach Rayleigh criterion with millimetre-scale resolution
